question: What error does the passage describe?
options: Confusing a rise in reported cases with a rise in actual cases

group.title: Reading comprehension
group.setup: A common error in reading statistics is to confuse a rise in reported cases with a rise in actual cases. When a district opens more testing centres, it will almost certainly record more cases of a disease, even if the disease is no more widespread than before. The same trap appears in crime figures, where better reporting can look like rising crime, and in bank fraud, where improved detection can make a careful bank look careless. The careful reader asks not only 'how many?' but also 'how was this counted, and has the method changed?'
